QING-QL-CONG-068  ·  ro-qing-068

Archaistic Cong-Form Vase with Turquoise Ground and Elephant-Head Handles

乾隆年製 (as claimed) — Qiánlóng Nián Zhì · Overglaze-Blue-Marked Famille Rose Porcelain, Qianlong Period (1736–1795)

Archaistic Cong Form Qing Dynasty · Qianlong 1736–1795 (claimed) Jingdezhen Imperial Kilns (claimed) Elephant-Head Handles Turquoise Ground & Overglaze-Blue Mark Dronova GOM Method

Object Description

The object photographed here is a square-bodied vase with gently rounded corners, in the archaistic cong form associated in Chinese ritual bronze and jade tradition with the ancient cosmological pairing of a round Heaven and a square Earth. The visible face carries a turquoise enamel ground densely overpainted with a symmetrical, hand-painted famille rose scrolling-lotus pattern — large stylised lotus blossoms in pink and cream with blue-and-purple leaf scrolls, rendered with fine dark contour lines and graduated petal shading (Fig. 3) — and an applied, sculptural elephant-head handle in iron-red enamel projects from the upper shoulder, its trunk curled and its eye and ear modelled in low relief (Fig. 4).

Only a partial side view, a base/mark view, and two close details (floral pattern and elephant handle) were supplied; no photograph shows the vase's full front elevation, its second handle, or its footring from a standard eye-level angle, so this entry describes what is directly visible in the four images rather than inferring the complete form.

The elephant-head handle shows individualised modelling of the trunk's curve and the visible eye and ear, with a slightly uneven, hand-worked surface texture rather than a perfectly smooth, mould-uniform finish; the join between the handle and the body is covered by the surrounding floral enamel rather than left as a visible raw seam, consistent with the handle having been fixed to the body before the overglaze enamel was applied.

Fig. 4 — Interior/base, showing the mark. A turquoise-glazed interior surface, with a fine, all-over craquelure network visible across the glaze, carries a mark in a square cartouche painted in a muted, dark grey-blue tone rather than the more saturated cobalt blue typically seen in underglaze reign marks elsewhere in this Atlas. The mark sits directly on top of the glaze rather than beneath it, consistent with the "overglaze blue enamel" mark type named in the accompanying notes and in the file name supplied with this image; the exact number and reading of the characters cannot be confirmed with confidence at this image resolution, and no claim beyond "present, overglaze, dark blue-grey" is made here about the mark's content.

Technological Interpretation

The turquoise ground shows a glossy, saturated surface in Fig. 1, and the fine craquelure network visible across the interior glaze in Fig. 4 is consistent with age-related crazing of a fired glaze, though craquelure pattern alone cannot be used to date an object and is reported here descriptively rather than as proof of age. The famille rose overpainting shows graduated petal shading and fine, individually drawn contour lines (Fig. 2) consistent with hand painting rather than a repeating transfer pattern, though this reading is based on standard photography rather than magnified examination.

Regarding the mark: the accompanying notes place particular emphasis on this piece carrying a rare overglaze-blue-enamel reign mark rather than the more common underglaze cobalt type, and note that such marks are less frequently encountered in Qianlong-period imperial production. The photograph (Fig. 4) is consistent with an overglaze application — the mark's colour and placement directly on the glazed surface differ visibly from the feathered, glaze-embedded underglaze cobalt marks documented elsewhere in this Atlas (compare, for example, the reign-mark micrograph in ro-qing-069). This entry records that visual distinction without independently confirming the mark's full six-character reading or its precise chemical composition.

The elephant-head handle's integration into the surrounding enamel, discussed above, is consistent with the handle having been modelled and attached before the final overglaze firing rather than added afterward; a proper joint-line examination at magnification would be needed to confirm this more rigorously.

Gemmological Optical Microscopy

The accompanying notes for this object contain extensive claims about features visible "under the microscope" or "under magnification" — glaze microbubble structure, multilayer enamel menisci, individual modelling and surface texture of the elephant handles, and the volume, granularity, and edge quality of the overglaze blue mark. No magnified or microscope photographs were supplied with this submission; only the four standard photographs reproduced above (Figs. 1–4) are available. Every microscope-level claim in the notes is therefore recorded here as unconfirmed, and this Atlas entry does not repeat them as independently verified findings.

No microscopy imagery available for this entry, despite extensive microscope-level claims in the accompanying notes. To document this object properly under the Dronova GOM Method, magnified images would be needed of: (1) the turquoise glaze, to assess genuine microbubble structure and age-related crazing; (2) the famille rose enamels, to assess layering and pigment granularity; (3) the elephant-head handle surface and its join to the body; and, most importantly given the object's distinguishing feature, (4) the overglaze-blue mark itself, to confirm its overglaze (rather than underglaze) placement, its pigment granularity, and its full character reading.

Diagnostic Checklist

  • Square, rounded-corner cong-form body, as far as visible in the supplied partial view
  • Saturated turquoise overglaze ground with a visible fine craquelure network on the interior
  • Hand-painted famille rose lotus scrollwork with graduated shading and individually drawn contour lines
  • Applied, individually modelled elephant-head handle integrated into the surrounding enamel
  • A mark painted directly on the glazed surface, visually consistent with the "overglaze blue enamel" type named in the accompanying notes
  • Mark's full six-character reading not legible with confidence from the supplied photograph
  • No photograph of the complete vessel, its second handle, or its footring supplied — overall form not independently confirmed
  • No microscopy imagery supplied — extensive microscope-level claims in the accompanying notes are not confirmed by this entry
  • No elemental (XRF/SEM-EDS) data yet obtained — the conclusion should be treated as preliminary at the chemical level
On the evidence of the four photographs supplied, the archaistic cong-type body, the turquoise famille rose ground, and the applied elephant-head handle are consistent with well-executed Qing-period decorative porcelain in the general style associated with Qianlong court taste. The mark, as photographed, is visually consistent with an overglaze (rather than underglaze) blue application — the specific, rarer feature emphasised in the accompanying notes — but its full six-character reading could not be confirmed at the resolution supplied, and this entry does not assert that reading as established fact. This is a partial documentation: no image of the complete standing vessel, the second handle, or the footring was provided, and the extensive microscope-level claims in the notes (glaze microbubbles, enamel meniscus structure, handle surface texture, mark pigment granularity) are not supported by any magnified image actually supplied. A conclusive attribution would require full-vessel photography, genuine magnified imagery — especially of the mark, given its stated rarity — and elemental analysis (XRF/SEM-EDS) of the glaze, enamels, and mark pigment.
